> Hello everyone,
>

>
> # Creates base phylogeny ~
> basePhylo2 <-
>   ggtree(Data2, layout = "fan", aes(colour = group), size = .125) +
>   scale_colour_manual(labels = c("Columba livia", "Columba rupestris"), values = c("#000000", "#fb8072"))
>
> # Merges annotation to base phylogeny ~
> basePhylo2_annot <- basePhylo2 %<+% Data2_annot
>
> # Creates final phylo ~
> basePhylo2_annot +
>   geom_fruit(
>     geom = geom_tile,
>     mapping = aes(y = label, x = BioStatus, fill = BioStatus),

x = 1 should solve this issue.

>     pwidth = .25)
>
>
>

messages.subject: Changing thickness of individual edges
messages.body_plain:
Hi y'all,

I'm trying to change the thickness of the branches in a phylogeny so that the branches in my clades of interest are thicker than those that are not. I've been able to get branches of multiple thicknesses, but unable to find a way to order my input dataframe so that the branches I want are the thickness I want. Any help is appreciated!

# generate dataframe of sizes for each edge
d2 <-
  data.frame(edge=0:(length(tree_pruned$edge.length+1)), size=0.05) %>%
  mutate(size = replace(size, edge %in% c(15:73, 804:860, 1355:1398, 1757:1803), 0.3))

# order dataframe, I've tried both of the methods below with no success
d2 <-
  d2[
  order( tree_pruned$edge[,1], tree_pruned$edge[,2] ),
]

d2 <- d2[ tree_pruned$edge[,2], ]

# generate initial tree
circ <-
  ggtree(tree_pruned, ladderize = T, layout = "circular", aes(size=d2$size), branch.length = "none") %<+% d + aes(color=I(color)) +
scale_color_manual(values=c("black", "#C0C0C0")) +
scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.05, 0.3))

# scale clades
  p1 <-  scaleClade(circ, node=1755, scale=7, vertical_only = T)
  p2 <-  scaleClade(p1, node=2027, scale=7, vertical_only = T)
  p3 <-  scaleClade(p2, node=1358, scale=7, vertical_only = T)
  p4 <-  scaleClade(p3, node=2226, scale=7, vertical_only = T)

# phylogeny

p6 +
 geom_strip(taxa1 = 401, taxa2 = 421, label = "Bacteroidota", offset.text = 1) +
 geom_strip(taxa1 = 691, taxa2 = 674, label = "Planctomycetota", offset.text = 3, hjust = 0.5) +
    geom_strip(taxa1 = 11, taxa2 = 15, label = "Proteobacteria", offset.text = 25) +
    geom_strip(taxa1 = 878, taxa2 = 898, label = "Patescibacteria", offset.text = 4, hjust = 0.5)

Thanks!

messages.subject: question about identify() / plotly functionality
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone, I am completely new to ggtree but am considering using it for my project. I'm excited about all of the annotation functionality that it has, and I was wondering about the identify method of generating an interactive phylogenetic tree.

I'm working on a meta-analysis of 18S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing data, and am phylogenetically placing these sequences into my reference tree to pull out the sequences that I'm interested in based on their phylogeny. I'm anticipating 1000s of sequences (not really sure on the amount, buy my reference tree has ~2000 sequences). What I want to be able to do is pull out the sequences I care about by highlighting them, and then output them either into a list of IDs, or use those to prune the tree. Is this possible using the idenitfy() method or by converting the tree to a plotly object? (also, if not, is anyone familiar with any other tools that might be of use? I'm interested in iTOL but most of the functionality I care about is behind a paywall)

Thank you!

If you could just give me a general suggestion as to where to start, that would be helpful. I cannot find any example where two layers of geom_tiplab are used in the same plot.

Best,
Dave
